Both have many versions. “Everything is imaginary” does not capture the full meaning of idealism.

This raises a question: how does a unified personal experience arise from experiences at smaller scales? This is called the combination problem; the D’Ariano–Faggin proposal also discusses it. [2]

Linguistic usefulness, social impact, and the writer’s feelings are three separate matters. The first two can have value even if the third has not been established.
Faggin-এর চিন্তা পড়ার সময় প্রশ্ন তুলুন:: When reading Faggin, ask whether his objection concerns a particular architecture of current digital computers or every possible artificial system. These claims require different scopes of evidence. Failure to establish consciousness in a current machine does not make it impossible for every future machine; equally, a good conversation is not sufficient evidence of consciousness.
